name: Wobbit

hardware_allowance.note: bearings, shoulder bolts, inserts, fasteners, wiring

notes: Defaults from the research: a 24 V-class 7S pack runs the J501 directly. The balance loop runs at 1 kHz on a microcontroller with CAN (the user's own board, to be chosen) or on the Jetson with a real-time kernel; the VN-100 Rugged is the balance IMU. The contactor cuts motor power only.

requirements: steady 1 kHz loop independent of Linux
2x CAN, or 1x CAN-FD, to the motors
UART (TTL or RS-232) for the VN-100
USB or Ethernet to the Jetson
options: a microcontroller with CAN (user's own board, to be named)
Linux real-time loop on the Jetson using the J501's native CAN-FD plus a hardware watchdog on the contactor (Upkie style)
balance_controller.status: open: waiting for the user's microcontroller list
